children: Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio) is drawing a sharp line between two software stocks benefiting from the AI boom, staying bullish on Veeva Systems
while calling Snowflake
very overvalued. The contrast comes as Snowflake shares surged more than
after another earnings beat, while Burry says Veeva's recent rally justified trimming his position without abandoning the broader investment thesis.

Veeva provides cloud software, data and consulting services to pharmaceutical and life-sciences companies. Its specialized platforms handle functions ranging from clinical trials and regulatory work to customer relationship management, giving the company a deeply embedded position in an industry with high switching costs.
Burry first disclosed his Veeva position in April and subsequently increased it, arguing that the beaten-down software stock remained cheap. After its recent rally, however, he reduced the position.
A stock that was recently beaten down rising very fast to a level of significant resistance/overhead pressure could lead me to trim the position. It would not lead me to sell it outright, Burry said.
Veeva's fundamentals have continued improving. Fiscal Q2 revenue climbed
18% to $928 million
, while GAAP operating income jumped
40% to $275 million
. Management raised its full-year revenue outlook to
$3.682 billion to $3.687 billion
, while Vault CRM adoption and new AI products remain major growth drivers.

Burry sees Snowflake very differently. He called the stock very overvalued and warned that companies could eventually keep more data in-house if cybersecurity concerns around centralized data platforms intensify.
That caution comes despite exceptional operating momentum. Snowflake's fiscal Q2 product revenue jumped
37% to $1.49 billion
, while total revenue rose
35% to $1.55 billion
. Remaining performance obligations reached
$9 billion
, and the company raised fiscal 2027 product revenue guidance to
$6.07 billion
, representing 36% growth.
Investors Takeaway
Burry's positioning highlights an important distinction between
business quality and entry price

Veeva is growing more slowly than Snowflake, but Burry appears willing to own it when valuation offers enough downside protection. Snowflake, meanwhile, is accelerating as enterprise AI demand expands, making timing a bearish call especially difficult.
For Veeva investors, watch subscription growth, Vault CRM adoption and operating margins. For Snowflake, the key question is whether product growth can stay near the
high-30% range
long enough to justify its elevated valuation.
If Snowflake's AI-driven acceleration persists, Burry's valuation concerns may take time to matter. But any sharp growth slowdown could quickly make valuation the dominant issue.

title: Michael Burry Warns Red-Hot AI Stock Is Overvalued
